title: ProRL: Prolonged Reinforcement Learning Expands Reasoning Boundaries in Large Language Models
one_line: Distilled 1.5B, >2k RL steps with KL resets; pass@128 from 256 samples; zero-base gains only on format-gated Reasoning Gym tasks; IFEval only in Fig. 3 and appendix.

title: ProRL (NeurIPS 2025 camera-ready)
one_line: Diffed against v1: §4 unchanged; adds a NeurIPS checklist (significance = pass@128 from 256 samples) and a pointer to the technical report and v2 blog.

title: Scaling LLM Reinforcement Learning with Prolonged Training Using ProRL v2
one_line: 3,000+ steps, REINFORCE++ baseline, resets every 200-500 steps; claims pass@k gains and base-always-fails breakthroughs with no k or numbers in text; IFEval only in a caption.

title: Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B model card
one_line: Default weights are v2 (3,000 steps; v1 needs revision v1); v2 IFEval 70.85 (average score); BroRL branch has 419 steps. Tells which ProRL third parties tested.

title: BroRL: Scaling Reinforcement Learning via Broadened Exploration
one_line: Continues the plateaued 3K-step ProRL v2 with 512 rollouts per prompt; 1-2 point pass@1 gains; no large-k or IF evaluation; pass@k only in theory.

title: When Pass@k Crossovers Are Real - and Why: Paired Inference and the Markov Kernel of RLVR
one_line: Paired re-test of ProRL-1.5B on 1,060 new maths problems: certified crossover (first loss k 12-63); log-odds slope 0.84, hard prompts gain on average; 2-3 % locked minority.

title: Scaling Up RL: Unlocking Diverse Reasoning in LLMs via Prolonged Training
one_line: ProRL technical report: KL control, clipping and resets as key ingredients, ablations; same pass@1 gains as v1; no new boundary test in the abstract.

title: The Invisible Leash: Why RLVR May or May Not Escape Its Origin
one_line: Re-tests ProRL at large k; covered by the IL agent, met here and not read.

title: RL Squeezes, SFT Expands: A Comparative Study of Reasoning LLMs
one_line: Covered by the IL agent; met here among ProRL citers, not read.

title: The Debate on RLVR Reasoning Capability Boundary: Shrinkage, Expansion, or Both? A Two-Stage Dynamic View
one_line: Theory and experiments: an early exploitation stage shrinks the boundary, a later exploration stage expands it; reconciles Yue and ProRL by training length.

title: The Reasoning Boundary Paradox: How Reinforcement Learning Constrains Language Models
one_line: Maths: RLVR reinforces problems already likely under the base and suppresses low-likelihood ones (winner-take-all), the opposite of largest-where-weakest at problem level.

title: Beyond Pass@k: Breadth-Depth Metrics for Reasoning Boundaries
one_line: Large-k pass@k on discrete answers rewards guessing; proposes Cover@tau; bears on our guessing control, not on ProRL tasks directly.

title: Curriculum Reinforcement Learning Can Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model
one_line: Teacher-guided curriculum lifts pass@256 by 9.8 points over bases; external guidance, so not plain-RL expansion.

title: How RL Reshapes LLM Reasoning: Transferability, Coverage, and Scaling Laws
one_line: Qwen and Gemma: large-budget coverage rises on some tasks and falls on others; a strategy-selection model explains both, like ProRL three regimes.

title: RL Grokking Recipe: How Does RL Unlock and Transfer New Algorithms in LLMs?
one_line: Code families with base pass@K = 0: long near-zero reward, then grokking with warm-up and curriculum; builds on prolonged RL for zero-to-one expansion.

title: JustRL: Scaling a 1.5B LLM with a Simple RL Recipe
one_line: Single-stage fixed-hyperparameter RL on 1.5B over 4,000+ steps without plateaus or resets; questions ProRL-style complexity; pass@1 only in the abstract.

title: QuestA: Expanding Reasoning Capacity in LLMs via Question Augmentation
one_line: Partial-solution hints during RL raise pass@k on hard maths for 1.5B models; augmentation, not a re-test of ProRL.

title: Nudging the Boundaries of LLM Reasoning
one_line: Self-generated hints unlock 0 %-pass training problems; pass@k gains; hint-based expansion relevant to prompt elicitation.

title: Scaling Behaviors of LLM Reinforcement Learning Post-Training: An Empirical Study in Mathematical Reasoning
one_line: Power laws for RL post-training across Qwen2.5 0.5-72B on maths; accuracy and test loss, no boundary measure.

title: Does Scaling Reinforcement Learning Really Require More Training?
one_line: Merges checkpoints of one RL history (incl. Nemotron/ProRL and OLMo) to beat its best checkpoint; accuracy, not reach.

title: Teacher-Free Self-Training Amplifies but Does Not Compound: A Pass@K Crossover on a Free-Verifier Domain
one_line: Self-training on a DSL wins at pass@8, the base overtakes at pass@64; no clean zero-capability frontier, so zero-then-climb tests are invalid there.

title: OMEGA: Can LLMs Reason Outside the Box in Math? Evaluating Exploratory, Compositional, and Transformative Generalization
one_line: Source benchmark of our OMEGA test_out reach (C5); exploratory, compositional and transformative splits; cites ProRL without re-testing it.

title: On the Interplay of Pre-Training, Mid-Training, and RL on Reasoning Language Models
one_line: Controlled pretraining: RL gains at pass@128 only with headroom and data at the edge of competence, a mechanism for largest-where-weak-but-not-zero.

title: Reinforcement Learning vs. Distillation: Understanding Accuracy and Capability in LLM Reasoning
one_line: RLVR raises accuracy on easier questions at the cost of the hardest (maths, small models), the reverse of ProRL pattern; predates ProRL.

title: Can GRPO Help LLMs Transcend Their Pretraining Origin?
one_line: Theory: GRPO is a conservative reweighting bounded by the base; from-scratch transformers gain OOD only when the task matches pretraining biases.

title: Depth-Breadth Synergy in RLVR: Unlocking LLM Reasoning Gains with Adaptive Exploration
one_line: GRPO down-weights hard problems; difficulty-adaptive rollouts raise pass@K; rollout size alone does not help, in contrast to BroRL.

title: DeepSearch: Overcome the Bottleneck of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Monte Carlo Tree Search
one_line: MCTS inside RLVR training to escape plateaus after thousands of steps; 5.7x fewer GPU-hours than extended training; accuracy only.

title: Locked at the Entrance, Open Inside: Where RLVR Narrows the Solution Space
one_line: Countdown: RLVR coverage loss concentrates at the first operation; entrance prefixes restore completions; SFT keeps more coverage.

title: Controlling Sharpening in LLM Post-Training
one_line: Closed-form KL-regularised pass@k and max@k optima shift pressure to hard prompts; KAPPO method; no ProRL re-test.

title: Differential Smoothing Mitigates Sharpening and Improves LLM Reasoning
one_line: Diversity-collapse theory and smoothing on correct trajectories; pass@k gains on Countdown and maths; not a boundary re-test.

title: Beyond Reasoning: Reinforcement Learning Unlocks Parametric Knowledge in LLMs
one_line: Closed-book QA: RL redistributes mass over known facts; items never answered in 128 pre-RL samples drive 83 % of the gain.

title: IsoCompute Playbook: Optimally Scaling Sampling Compute for LLM RL
one_line: Compute-optimal rollouts per problem rise then saturate; coverage expansion on hard problems; frames BroRL rollout axis.

title: Limits of Generalization in RLVR: Two Case Studies in Mathematical Reasoning
one_line: Scheduling and longest-increasing-subsequence: RLVR improves metrics by reinforcing superficial heuristics rather than new strategies.

title: Understanding Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning: Broader Reasoning Coverage than GRPO
one_line: Evolution strategies keep higher pass@K than GRPO via diversity; method comparison, no ProRL re-test.

title: From Trial-and-Error to Improvement: A Systematic Analysis of LLM Exploration Mechanisms in RLVR
one_line: Technical report on exploration metrics and entropy-performance trade-offs; no ProRL re-test.

title: Beyond Accuracy: Dissecting Mathematical Reasoning for LLMs Under Reinforcement Learning
one_line: SPARKLE analysis of plan following and knowledge integration under RL; scaffolds hard problems; not a boundary re-test.
